title: Heteroskedasticity of unknown form (González-Coya and Perron, 2024)
text: \(\mathrm{Var}(u_t) = v_t\) varies across observations, weighted least squares weights \(1/v_t\) efficient. variances unknown functional form rarely known. approach 2024 paper: run OLS form \(r_t = \log \max(\hat u_t^2, \delta^2)\), floor \(\delta = 0.1\) (delta, units \(y\)) avoids \(\log 0\); regress \(r_t\) dictionary candidate covariates \(z_t\) adaptive Lasso. ridge regression gives weights \(|\hat\gamma^{ridge}_j|^{-\psi}\), penalty \(\lambda\) exponent \(\psi \\{0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 2\}\) chosen jointly 10-fold cross-validation, folds every \(\psi\); use \(\exp(\hat r_t)\) variances weighted least squares. skedastic model approximation, variance \(\hat\beta\) sandwich (eq. 6) bias correction estimated weights (eq. 8). Confidence intervals therefore remain valid model \(v_t\) wrong.

title: Serial correlation (Perron and González-Coya, 2026)
text: \(y_t = x_t'\beta + u_t\) autocorrelated errors, GLS (feasible version) efficient OLS. classic feasible version, Cochrane-Orcutt, estimates error autocorrelation OLS residuals. fine regressors exogenous, uncorrelated errors leads lags. Many time-series regressors pre-determined: uncorrelated current future innovations, respond past ones, policy variables, expectations lagged prices. OLS inconsistent, Cochrane-Orcutt, inherits residuals.

title: Serial correlation (Perron and González-Coya, 2026)
text: errors approximated AR(k) process, \(u_t = \rho_1 u_{t-1} + \dots + \rho_k u_{t-k} + e_t\). Substituting \(u_t = y_t - x_t'\beta\) gives Durbin regression \[y_t = \sum_{j=1}^k \rho_j y_{t-j} + x_t'\beta - \sum_{j=1}^k x_{t-j}'\delta_j + e_t ,\] estimated OLS. Every regressor equation uncorrelated innovation \(e_t\) \(x_t\) pre-determined, coefficients lagged \(y\) estimate \(\rho_j\) consistently. fgls: order \(k\) minimizes BIC \(0, \dots, k_{max}\), orders fitted sample (eq. 14); data quasi-differenced estimated filter, every column including constant, first \(k\) observations dropped; OLS filtered data gives \(\hat\beta\) (eq. 15). Lagged columns duplicate regressors (lags constant, linear trend, periodic dummies) dropped automatically Durbin regression.

title: Serial correlation (Perron and González-Coya, 2026)

title: Serial correlation (Perron and González-Coya, 2026)
text: lags \(y\) regressors, Durbin coefficients lagged \(y\) mix dynamics model errors. common-factor structure AR coefficients can recovered ratio lagged regressor’s coefficient contemporaneous one (Wallis, 1967; Section 4.2 paper). Declare lagged dependent variables: Without declaration, fgls() warns regressor looks like lagged dependent variable.
code: set.seed(3) n <- 400 w <- rnorm(n + 1) u <- as.numeric(stats::filter(rnorm(n + 1), 0.5, method = "recursive")) yy <- numeric(n + 1) for (t in 2:(n + 1)) yy[t] <- 0.4 * yy[t - 1] + 1 + w[t] + u[t] dyn <- data.frame(y = yy[-1], ylag = yy[-(n + 1)], w = w[-1]) fit_dyn <- serial_fgls(y ~ ylag + w, data = dyn, lagged_dep_vars = "ylag") coef(fit_dyn) #> (Intercept)        ylag           w  #>   0.8010813   0.4491766   1.0389021 fit_dyn$rho #>      rho1  #> 0.4586741
